title: AI helped me build local co-op for my Unity car combat game – but it definitely wasn’t “one prompt and done” Added local co-op to my solo-developed car combat game, Brutal Derby.
author: Dense-Bar-2341
selftext:
The game has been built in Unity with AI heavily involved in the development workflow, and local multiplayer turned out to be one of the more interesting systems to implement.

Two players can now play together locally, while the arenas still have AI opponents, weapons, pickups, destruction and all the usual chaos.

I’m trying to use AI for actual production work rather than just generating a quick prototype, and this project keeps reminding me how much integration, testing and manual work is still needed even with AI helping.

Brutal Derby is still in development, but local co-op is finally working.

For other AI-assisted solo devs: have you tried implementing split-screen or local multiplayer with AI coding tools? How much did they actually help?

Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/5083440/BRUTAL\_DERBY/
